bug_semantics: Stored same-origin XSS in the Form node completion page: renderFormCompletion always retrieved responseText and passed it to packages/cli/templates/form-trigger-completion.handlebars, whose triple-brace {{{responseText}}} sink rendered attacker HTML verbatim. Commit 7f651ca5a3162ba0f13242dc934047e32998b33c changed the formerly unconditional sandbox Content-Security-Policy into a respondWith !== 'redirect' conditional without also suppressing responseText for redirect responses. An authenticated member could retain populated responseText while making the expression-capable respondWith parameter evaluate to redirect; a public-form submitter then received the raw HTML without the sandbox CSP, so script ran from the n8n origin with the visitor's session context.
flaw_origin: The smallest causal change is 7f651ca5a3162ba0f13242dc934047e32998b33c (fix(n8n Form Node): CSP headers should not be set on response with redirect (#20864)). It introduced a local respondWith variable and guarded res.setHeader('Content-Security-Policy', SANDBOX_CSP) with respondWith !== 'redirect', while deliberately leaving the pre-existing unconditional responseText read and raw template sink intact. This newly created the exploitable combination; it is a focused two-file implementation/test commit, not a move, refactor, revert, release/backport, or broad squash aggregate.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p 7f651ca5a3162ba0f13242dc934047e32998b33c identifies human author Michael Kret <88898367+michael-radency@users.noreply.github.com> and committer GitHub <noreply@github.com>; the commit message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Made-with, or other AI trailer, and neither identity is an AI coding bot.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/security/advisories/GHSA-rmr5-775f-jvm2 describes the exact redirect-expression/raw-responseText sandbox bypass and its same-origin session impact; its affected-version table gives <1.123.69, <2.33.4, and <2.34.1 (the older numbers still present in its prose Patches paragraph are contradicted by both that table and the repository trees). In the validated clone, `git show 7f651ca5a3162ba0f13242dc934047e32998b33c -- packages/nodes-base/nodes/Form/utils/formCompletionUtils.ts packages/nodes-base/nodes/Form/test/formCompletionUtils.test.ts` shows responseText remaining unconditional while the CSP changes from unconditional to `if (respondWith !== 'redirect')`; `git grep -n responseText 7f651ca5a3162ba0f13242dc934047e32998b33c -- packages/cli/templates/form-trigger-completion.handlebars` finds lines 108-109 `{{#if responseText}}` and `{{{responseText}}}`. `git show f527ae125233064c9f6a1293dd5e34e4a1b0a4b7:packages/nodes-base/nodes/Form/utils/formCompletionUtils.ts` directly verifies the immediate parent still reads raw responseText but unconditionally sets SANDBOX_CSP, so the bypass is absent there. `git log master -L 96,105:packages/nodes-base/nodes/Form/utils/formCompletionUtils.ts` traces the eventual responseText gating, and `git log --all -S"if (respondWith !== 'redirect')" -- packages/nodes-base/nodes/Form/utils/formCompletionUtils.ts` identifies 7f651ca5a3162ba0f13242dc934047e32998b33c as the first conditional-CSP writer (later matches only amend the condition for an administrator-controlled sandbox-disable setting). `git diff n8n@1.116.2 n8n@1.117.0 --` the same implementation/test files reproduces the BIC patch, and `git tag --contains 7f651ca5a3162ba0f13242dc934047e32998b33c --list 'n8n@1.*' --sort=version:refname` starts at n8n@1.117.0. Closing master fix ca3d42d8386515cd9f044377a15a632cd09b62f0 changes responseText to be read only when respondWith === 'showText', otherwise '', and its redirect regression test asserts responseText: ''. Equivalent branch landings are 3e4fb19caf73276a68b38d45d96b3da5baf7cab7 (1.x), 0405fc550f55051f6c459252f5860fa78d27ab80 (2.33.x), and 170cfc787015d352488f6b6403af07a74e95ca1d (2.34.x). `git diff n8n@1.123.68 n8n@1.123.69`, `git diff n8n@2.33.3 n8n@2.33.4`, and `git diff n8n@2.34.0 n8n@2.34.1` on formCompletionUtils.ts each reproduce that gate; `git tag --contains` for the three branch fixes starts respectively at n8n@1.123.69, n8n@2.33.4, and n8n@2.34.1. Finally, `git cat-file -p 7f651ca5a3162ba0f13242dc934047e32998b33c` supplies the exact human author/committer identities and confirms the complete absence of AI attribution trailers on the BIC object.
reasoning: Before the BIC, responseText was already intentionally raw HTML, but the completion response always received SANDBOX_CSP; therefore attacker script was confined to the sandbox rather than executing as the n8n origin. The BIC's security-relevant new behavior was specifically to omit that sandbox whenever the resolved respondWith value was redirect. Because renderFormCompletion still fetched and rendered responseText independently of respondWith, an expression-resolved redirect could coexist with stored raw HTML even though the editor's ordinary display rules presented those choices as mutually exclusive. Direct parent-tree inspection proves this exploitable combination did not exist one commit earlier, and -L/-S plus the 1.116.2-to-1.117.0 tag diff rule out a later move or backport as the origin. The August 2026 closing patch keeps redirects unsandboxed but removes their raw payload by setting responseText to the empty string unless showText is selected; the three maintenance-line tag diffs establish the final fixed boundaries. The BIC itself is authored by a named human, committed by GitHub, and has no commit-object AI marker. Bot authorship on the later bundled fix is irrelevant under the BIC-only attribution rule, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
